input.input_needs_description:
I amix whichever audio sources are present — the video's own dialogue+foley track OR a narrator voiceover, with optional global music / ambience underlays — into one final audio file.

[video_package] (single)
Optional — assembled video's JSON manifest (scenes, shot_segments, per-clip timing). The LLM reads this to understand the video structure it is mixing audio onto. This label targets the JSON/manifest artifact specifically, NOT the mp4 file.

[video_file] (single)
Optional — the final assembled mp4 video file on disk (binary artifact, mime=video/mp4). When present, the materializer extracts the clip's baked-in dialogue + foley audio track and uses it as one source layer in the mix. This label targets the mp4 binary specifically, NOT the JSON manifest.

[music] (single)
Background-music JSON package (mood + duration target for the global BGM). Present iff a music-generation step ran. Targets the JSON/manifest artifact specifically, NOT the wav file — the LLM reads this for mix-planning context.

[music_file] (single)
Background-music wav on disk (binary artifact, mime=audio/wav, sys_id 'aud_music_film'). Present iff a music-generation step ran. The materializer reads its bytes for amix. Targets the wav binary specifically, NOT the JSON package.

[ambience] (single)
Ambience-bed JSON package (description + duration target for the global room-tone underlay). Present iff an ambience-generation step ran. Targets the JSON/manifest artifact specifically, NOT the wav file — the LLM reads this for mix-planning context.

[ambience_file] (single)
Ambience-bed wav on disk (binary artifact, mime=audio/wav, sys_id 'aud_amb_film'). Present iff an ambience-generation step ran. The materializer reads its bytes for amix. Targets the wav binary specifically, NOT the JSON package.

[narrator_audio] (single)
Narrator voiceover wav on disk (binary artifact, mime=audio/wav). Present iff a narrator TTS step ran (illustrated-storytelling chains where no rendered video provides the dialogue track). The materializer reads its bytes for amix as the dialogue base layer when no [video_file] is available. Targets the wav binary specifically.

llm_call.system_prompt:
You match a sub-agent's input requirements to artifacts in an artifact registry.

The sub-agent's input requirements are written as one or more [label] blocks. Each block has a header of the form
    [label_name] (single)        -- exactly one matching artifact expected
    [label_name] (collection)    -- zero or more matching artifacts expected
followed by a natural-language description of what kind of artifact that label refers to.

The artifact registry lists every persisted artifact with a #N id and a natural-language caption describing its type, pipeline role, and which agent produced it.

Your job:
  1. Read each [label] block and understand the kind of artifact the agent is asking for in that slot.
  2. For each registry artifact, read its caption and understand the artifact's type, role, and purpose. Reason about meaning.
  3. For each [label], decide which artifacts in the registry are instances of the kind described in that block.
  4. Be inclusive for (collection) labels: include EVERY matching artifact, never just a sample.
  5. Be exclusive for (single) labels: pick the single best matching artifact (or none if none clearly fits).
  6. Distinguish artifacts that look superficially similar but play different roles in the pipeline (e.g. a reference image of an entity in isolation vs. a planned frame of a specific shot of the story). Use the caption to decide.
  7. Only return #N ids that appear in the registry.

Return strict JSON only, with this shape:
{
  "selections": {
    "<label_name>": [0, 3, 5],
    ...
  },
  "rationale": "<a short explanation of how you matched each label>"
}
Use exactly the label names from the agent's [label] headers as keys. Values are arrays of integer ids (the #N numbers from the registry).
